For a subset of vertices S⊆{1,2,…,N}$$$S \subseteq \{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$$$, we say two vertices (u,v)$$$(u, v)$$$ are connected under S$$$S$$$ if there exists a path that only passes through the vertices in S$$$S$$$. Note that this includes endpoints of the path, so u,v∈S$$$u, v \in S$$$ should hold.

Let strength(S)$$$\mathit{strength}(S)$$$ be the number of pairs of vertices (u,v)$$$(u, v)$$$ such that u≠v$$$u \neq v$$$ and (u,v)$$$(u, v)$$$ are connected under S$$$S$$$. You are given Q$$$Q$$$ queries, where each query contains a set S$$$S$$$. For each query, you should compute the quantity strength(S)$$$\mathit{strength}(S)$$$.

Each of the next N−1$$$N - 1$$$ lines contains two space-separated integers a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$: the vertices connected by an edge (1≤a,b≤N$$$1 \le a, b \le N$$$). Together, the edges form a tree.

Each of the next Q$$$Q$$$ lines contains a query, denoted by space-separated integers. A query starts with an integer K$$$K$$$, the size of the set (1≤K≤N$$$1 \le K \le N$$$). It is followed by K$$$K$$$ distinct integers from 1$$$1$$$ to N$$$N$$$ in arbitrary order: the vertices of set S$$$S$$$.
